issues.legal_issue: A civil court must refer a tenancy issue to the competent authority when the issue arises in a civil suit and the law assigns its determination to that authority, even if the issue arises incidentally.
material_facts: The landlords leased the land to the respondents’ predecessor, and later sued for possession after the lease ended.
The respondents disputed the civil court’s jurisdiction and contended that the tenancy legislation applied to the land.
The High Court remanded the suit with directions to refer any issues reserved for the competent authority, including tenancy issues, for determination.
issues.conclusion: The High Court correctly directed the trial court to refer any issue required to be determined exclusively by the competent authority and to dispose of the suit in accordance with that authority’s decision.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 70(b), 85 and 85A of the Bombay Tenancy and Agricultural Lands Act, 1948, as amended to include whether a person was at any time in the past a tenant, a civil court cannot determine an assigned tenancy issue, even if it arises incidentally, and must refer it to the competent authority. The court relies on G.S. Shinde v. R.B. Joshi and Bhimaji Shanker Kulkarni v. Dundappa Vithappa Udapudi; it explains that Mussamiya Imam Haider Bax Razvi v. Rabari Govindhai Ratnabhai concerned the earlier statutory position.

predicates.civil_suit_involves_tenancy_issue: A party to a civil suit raises a dispute about whether a person is or was a tenant.
predicates.law_assigns_issue_to_special_authority: The law assigns determination of that tenancy issue to a competent specialist authority rather than the civil court.

issues.definition: When a civil suit raises a tenancy issue assigned by law to a specialist authority, the issue must be referred to that authority.

issues.legal_issue: An earlier ex parte summary possession proceeding that did not directly and substantially decide tenancy status does not bar a later civil court reference of the tenancy issue on res judicata grounds.
material_facts: Before bringing the civil suit, the landlords applied to the tenancy authority for possession under the tenancy legislation.
The authority dismissed that application ex parte, stating that the land grew natural grass and that it lacked jurisdiction to order possession.
The landlords then brought the civil suit, and the tenancy issue in that suit had not been contested and finally decided in the earlier proceeding.
issues.conclusion: The earlier order did not create a res judicata bar to the trial court referring tenancy issues to the competent authority.
issues.legal_principle: Section 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure bars a matter only when it was directly and substantially in issue and was heard and finally decided; what binds is the ratio fundamental to the decision, not an extension by logical inference. An ex parte proceeding ordinarily determines only the relief claimed, and a summary application need not qualify as a suit for Section 11. A court lacking jurisdiction cannot confer jurisdiction on itself by an erroneous decision, and its jurisdictional ruling does not operate as res judicata. The court relies on Vithal Yaswant v. Shikander Khan Mutumukhtan, Pandurang Mahadeo Kavade v. Annaji Balwant Bokil, Bhagwan Dayal v. Mst. Reoti Devi, and the principles discussed in Duchess of Kingston’s case.

rule.if: current_civil_suit_involves_tenancy_issue and prior_summary_possession_application and prior_decision_was_ex_parte and prior_authority_declined_jurisdiction and tenancy_status_was_not_contested_and_finally_decided

predicates.current_civil_suit_involves_tenancy_issu: A civil suit raises a dispute about whether a person is or was a tenant.
predicates.prior_summary_possession_application: Before the civil suit, a party sought possession through a summary application to an authority.
predicates.prior_decision_was_ex_parte: The authority decided the earlier application without the opposing party appearing.
predicates.prior_authority_declined_jurisdiction: The authority dismissed the earlier application on the ground that it lacked power to order possession.
predicates.tenancy_status_was_not_contested_and_fin: The earlier proceeding did not hear and finally decide, as a contested matter, whether the opposing party was a tenant.

issues.definition: If a civil suit raises a tenancy issue after an ex parte summary possession application in which the authority declined jurisdiction and tenancy status was not contested and finally decided, the earlier decision does not bar reference of the tenancy issue.
